board_events.text: Subtopic 3 — the traps, and the decode-first discipline
AOI-MOD-CORNER: every modulus has a kink — set each inside to zero and split. Nested $||x|-1|$ has two.
AOI-INEQ-SIDE: translate ≤ / ≥ carefully and confirm with a test point (often the origin).
AOI-COMPOSITE-SPLIT: when the ceiling switches, one integral cannot cover both slabs.
AOI-SYMM-MISS: symmetry is a gift only after you verify it — then remember to multiply back.
Pro-tip: spend 30 seconds turning the problem into a labelled sketch first.
Pro-tip: use elementary geometry (diamonds, wedges, sectors) as a free cross-check.
Almost every lost mark here is a decoding error, not an integration error.

segments.text: Let's close the advanced subtopic with its traps and the one discipline that prevents them all.

The first trap is missing a corner of a modulus curve. Every modulus contributes a kink, so set each inside-expression to zero and split there. A nested modulus like mod, mod x minus one, has two corners — miss one and your limits are wrong.

Second, shading the wrong side of an inequality. Translate the less-than-or-equal and greater-than-or-equal carefully, and confirm with a test point — the origin is easiest whenever it is not on a boundary.
Third, forgetting to split a composite region. When the top boundary switches partway across, a single integral cannot cover both slabs — you must split at the switch point.
Fourth, assuming symmetry that isn't there, or forgetting to multiply back after using it. Symmetry is a gift only after you have verified it.

<curious> The first pro-tip: spend the first thirty seconds turning the problem into a labelled sketch — corners marked, sides shaded, switch points found. Once the picture is right, the integral is the easy part.

The second pro-tip: use elementary geometry as a free check. Diamonds, wedges, sectors, and triangles have simple shape-formula areas. Compute the answer both ways; if they disagree, you mis-decoded the boundary.
Hold the one big lesson of this subtopic close: almost every lost mark here is a decoding error, not an integration error. Decode the boundary carefully, and the calculus is the easy part.
चलो advanced subtopic को इसके traps और उस एक discipline के साथ बंद करें जो इन सबको रोकती है।

पहला trap है एक modulus curve का corner miss करना। हर modulus एक kink देता है, तो हर inside-expression को zero रखो और वहाँ split करो। mod, mod x minus one, जैसे nested modulus के दो corners होते हैं — एक miss करो और तुम्हारे limits गलत हैं।

दूसरा, एक inequality की गलत side shade करना। less-than-or-equal और greater-than-or-equal को ध्यान से translate करो, और एक test point से confirm करो — origin सबसे आसान है जब भी यह किसी boundary पर न हो।
तीसरा, एक composite region split करना भूल जाना। जब top boundary बीच में switch करे, एक single integral दोनों slabs cover नहीं कर सकता — तुम्हें switch point पर split करना होगा।
चौथा, ऐसी symmetry मान लेना जो है ही नहीं, या इसे use करने के बाद वापस multiply करना भूल जाना। symmetry एक gift है सिर्फ़ verify करने के बाद।
<curious> पहली pro-tip: पहले तीस सेकंड problem को एक labelled sketch में बदलने में लगाओ — corners marked, sides shaded, switch points found। एक बार picture सही हो, integral आसान हिस्सा है।

दूसरी pro-tip: elementary geometry को एक free check की तरह use करो। diamonds, wedges, sectors, और triangles की simple shape-formula areas होती हैं। answer दोनों तरीकों से निकालो; अगर वे disagree करें, तुमने boundary गलत decode की।
इस subtopic का एक बड़ा सबक पास रखो: यहाँ लगभग हर lost mark एक decoding error है, integration error नहीं। boundary ध्यान से decode करो, और calculus आसान हिस्सा है।

sections.title: Chapter 8 — the complete area toolkit

board_events.text: Every formula from all three subtopics, in one place

board_events.latex: \text{Curves that cross:}\;\; A = \int_a^b |f - g|\,dx \;\;(\text{split at the swap})

board_events.text: Method select: one curve + axis → Sub-1; two curves → Sub-2; modulus / inequality / region → Sub-3.

segments.text: Here is the complete area toolkit for the whole chapter, gathered on one board. This is a recap — we're restating, not re-teaching, so let each formula trigger the reasoning you already own.
For a curve against an axis: the area is the integral of y d x, or, measured against the y-axis, the integral of x d y.
When the curve dips below or crosses the axis: the area is the integral of the absolute value of f, splitting at every root so nothing cancels.
For the area between two curves: top minus bottom integrated in x, or equivalently right minus left integrated in y.
When the two curves cross inside the interval: the area is the integral of the absolute value of f minus g, splitting at each swap.
The catalogue results worth memorising: the circle gives pi a squared, the ellipse pi a b, the two equal parabolas sixteen a squared over three, and the diamond two a squared.
And the workhorse antiderivative that powers every circle, ellipse, and cap problem: the integral of root a squared minus x squared.

<excited> The method-selection guide is the compass for the whole chapter: one curve plus an axis is a Subtopic-one problem, two named curves is Subtopic two, and anything with a modulus, an inequality, or a region in braces is a Subtopic-three decoding problem. Choose the right subtopic and the rest is routine.

यह रहा पूरे chapter का complete area toolkit, एक board पर इकट्ठा। यह एक recap है — हम restate कर रहे हैं, फिर से नहीं पढ़ा रहे, तो हर formula को वो reasoning trigger करने दो जो तुम्हारे पास पहले से है।
एक axis के against curve के लिए: area है integral of y d x, या, y-axis के against मापी जाए तो, integral of x d y।
जब curve axis के नीचे झुके या cross करे: area है f की absolute value का integral, हर root पर split करते हुए ताकि कुछ cancel न हो।
दो curves के बीच की area के लिए: x में integrate किया top minus bottom, या equivalently y में integrate किया right minus left।
जब दोनों curves interval के अंदर cross करें: area है f minus g की absolute value का integral, हर swap पर split करते हुए।
memorise करने लायक catalogue results: circle देता है pi a squared, ellipse pi a b, दो equal parabolas sixteen a squared over three, और diamond two a squared।
और वो workhorse antiderivative जो हर circle, ellipse, और cap problem चलाता है: integral of root a squared minus x squared।

<excited> method-selection guide पूरे chapter का compass है: एक curve plus एक axis एक Subtopic-one problem है, दो named curves Subtopic two है, और modulus, inequality, या braces में एक region वाली कोई भी चीज़ Subtopic-three decoding problem है। सही subtopic चुनो और बाकी routine है।

sections.title: Chapter 8 master cheat sheet

board_events.text: Fast recall: the whole chapter on one page
Curve & axis: $A = \int_a^b y\,dx$ or $\int_c^d x\,dy$ — pick the variable by the geometry.
Below / crossing the axis: $A = \int |f|\,dx$ — split at every root.
Between curves: $\int$ (top − bottom) $dx$; limits = intersection points (solve $f = g$).
Curves that cross: split at the swap, integrate $|f - g|$.
Standard: circle $\pi a^2$, ellipse $\pi ab$, two parabolas $\tfrac{16a^2}{3}$, diamond $2a^2$.
Modulus / inequality / region: decode → sketch → split → integrate; geometry is a free check.
Universal routine: Sketch → Limits → Pick variable ($dx$/$dy$) → Integrate (with |·|, splitting, symmetry).

segments.text: Finally, the master cheat sheet — the whole chapter on one page, the kind of thing to skim minutes before an exam.
Curve against an axis: the area is the integral of y d x, or x d y — and you pick the variable to match the geometry, d x for walled left and right, d y for capped top and bottom.
Below or crossing the axis: integrate the absolute value of f, and split at every root so positive and negative pieces never cancel.
Between two curves: integrate top minus bottom, and remember the limits are the intersection points, found by solving f equals g first.
When the curves cross: split at the swap and integrate the absolute value of f minus g.
The standard results: circle pi a squared, ellipse pi a b, two equal parabolas sixteen a squared over three, and the diamond two a squared.
And for a modulus, an inequality, or a region in braces: decode, sketch, split, and integrate — always using elementary geometry as a free cross-check.

<whisper> Carry the universal routine through every single problem: Sketch, then Limits from intersections or corners, then Pick the variable d x or d y, then Integrate with absolute values, splitting, and symmetry. Top minus bottom, every strip, every time — and decode the boundary, because the calculus is the easy part.
आख़िर में, master cheat sheet — पूरा chapter एक page पर, exam से मिनटों पहले skim करने लायक चीज़।
एक axis के against curve: area है integral of y d x, या x d y — और तुम variable को geometry से match करने के लिए चुनते हो, left-right walled के लिए d x, top-bottom capped के लिए d y।
axis के नीचे या cross करते: f की absolute value integrate करो, और हर root पर split करो ताकि positive और negative pieces कभी cancel न हों।
दो curves के बीच: top minus bottom integrate करो, और याद रखो limits intersection points हैं, पहले f equals g solve करके पाए गए।
जब curves cross करें: swap पर split करो और f minus g की absolute value integrate करो।
standard results: circle pi a squared, ellipse pi a b, दो equal parabolas sixteen a squared over three, और diamond two a squared।
और एक modulus, एक inequality, या braces में एक region के लिए: decode, sketch, split, और integrate — हमेशा elementary geometry को एक free cross-check की तरह use करते हुए।

<whisper> universal routine को हर एक problem में ले जाओ: Sketch, फिर intersections या corners से Limits, फिर variable d x या d y Pick करो, फिर absolute values, splitting, और symmetry के साथ Integrate। top minus bottom, हर strip, हर बार — और boundary decode करो, क्योंकि calculus आसान हिस्सा है।
